JM Next-Gen 2028 Jeep Wrangler Arrives Early for a First Look, Though Only Across Imagination Land
27 photos
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube
In case you haven’t noticed, Jeep has been pretty busy lately, as it aims to bring out enough novelties to regain the leadership position among Stellantis brands in America, after it lost the throne recently to Ram Trucks. As such, we have already seen a ton of novelties.
Those include the 2027 Compass, 2027 Gladiator, 2027 Wrangler, 2027 Cherokee, the new 35-inch Tire Launch Edition for the Gladiator, or the 2027 Switchback that completed in a very cool way the year-long Twelve 4 Twelve campaign series of limited editions for the Wrangler nameplate. Oh, and Jeep was also named the official 4x4 of the city of Moab, among others.
How about the 2026 SEMA Show event in Las Vegas, Nevada? Of course, Mopar fans had things to do there – including admiring the Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept, the prototype model from specialty brand Jeep with an SRT badge. But what could be cooler than the reimagining of the American off-road icon, the legendary Jeep CJ-8 Scrambler?
Well, according to the rumor mill, perhaps a brand-new iteration of the iconic Jeep Wrangler might do the trick. With a little help from a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators who stops dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, of course. So, the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube have unofficially imagined the CGI look of the all-new 2028 Jeep Wrangler off-road SUV – either for the ‘JM’ iteration or as a second refresh.
The channel’s host muses that in 2027 we should be expecting either the reveal of an all-new generation following in the footsteps of the YJ (1987), TJ (1997), JK (2007), and JL (2018), or a second refresh that could extend its life a little further, through the 2029 model year. Since the Wrangler Scrambler was recently announced at the 2026 SEMA Show, it could partially follow its design lead, of course.
The news outlet wants to preview the 2028 or 2029 Jeep Wrangler JM look way ahead of its official release, and the host passes the baton to the resident virtual artist to show us their interpretation of the exterior and interior of a new 4-door Wrangler Unlimited model. It comes directly inspired by the Scrambler with new headlights and the new seven-slot grille style, plus massive off-road wheels and tires.
There are also fresh colors – something that Jeep has always been known for. The profile isn’t too different, though, only subtly improved, along with the rear LED taillights. Inside, the Wrangler could retain the current dashboard layout but with several improvements: a new square steering wheel, a fully digital instrument cluster, and a larger central infotainment screen with integrated but physical controls for the climate system. Cool or not?

Tow Côja Tiny Home Is a Rustic Retreat With Three Double Beds and a Charming Rooftop Deck
12 photos
Photo: Madeiguincho
Some people choose to live tiny to gain financial freedom, others are into it for the sustainability factor, and others are simply looking for personal liberation. But regardless of the reason behind their decision, tiny home living isn’t just a trend anymore. It has become a lifestyle, a deliberate choice towards simplicity and sustainable living.
Even though, lately, tiny houses have been getting bigger and more luxurious in some parts of the world, there are still builders who craft simple, practical tiny homes that allow dwellers to embrace a minimalist, less consumption-oriented lifestyle. One of them is Madeiguincho, a Portugal-based woodworking and architecture atelier that focused on craftsmanship, sustainable timber construction, and spatial efficiency.
The studio has been around since 1990 and builds absolutely stunning wooden tiny houses that feel right at home in any natural environment. This builder’s models are not just a place to live or a shelter, but a place of comfort where you can live more in harmony with the surrounding nature.
This talented team’s latest creation is Tow Côja, a tiny house on wheels designed as a minimalist, peaceful retreat that exudes rustic cabin vibes and proves that, when thoughtfully used, space is more than just a number. Though it has a footprint of only 17 square meters (183 square feet), this compact dwelling holds more than you might expect.
Photo: Madeiguincho It boasts a dual-loft layout and can perfectly serve as a retreat for family vacations, as it can accommodate up to six people in its three double beds. It also includes an open living room, a kitchen, and a bathroom. But with two glass double doors, large windows, and a rooftop deck, this is a tiny home that not only keeps you connected to your surroundings but also encourages you to spend time outside.
Built on a dual-axle trailer, this compact dwelling can be towed to your preferred spot in nature and also offers the possibility of relocation. Its exterior is clad in dark burnt wood, giving the home a traditional, rustic appearance, and multiple windows with natural wood frames break up the dark facade on both levels, adding a warmer touch and allowing ample daylight to filter inside.
But the most distinctive feature when viewed from the outside is the split roof design. Two elevated roof sections add architectural interest and flank a recessed central area that has been configured as a wooden rooftop deck. Accessible from the upper level of the tiny home, this terrace provides a nice spot to relax and enjoy panoramic views of the surroundings.
Photo: Madeiguincho One of the glass entry doors leads into the central kitchen area, while the second one opens the living room to the outside. Both keep the interior open, bright, and airy, allowing for seamless indoor-outdoor living, something that many tiny home dwellers are looking for.
Tow Côja’s interior exudes a cabin feel, with an exquisite rustic aesthetic that combines several types of natural wood, including birch plywood panels, cedar, pine wood, and more. Environmentally friendly, durable, and high-quality, the different types of timber that adorn the interior walls, ceiling, and floors help create a warm and cozy ambiance.
The layout is open-plan and highly functional, maximizing the limited square footage. The kitchen occupies the center of the house, flanked by the living room on the left and the bathroom on the right. Simple wood ladders provide access to the two lofts, each positioned at either end of the house.
Photo: Madeiguincho The living room is bathed in natural light and is kept simple and minimalist , with just a built-in sofa bench with integrated storage and custom cushions. But that’s the setup during the day, because at night, the space transforms into a sleeping space thanks to a Murphy bed that’s neatly integrated next to the sofa. It stays flush against the wall when not needed, leaving ample room to move around, but it’s there when you want an extra bed.
A classic black cast-iron wood-burning stove is included between the living area and the kitchen. Placed on a protective floor plate, it adds another rustic touch, contributing to the cozy, warm atmosphere.
Minimalist in design but complete in terms of functionality, the kitchen is aligned against one wall and stands out with its country aesthetic featuring plywood cabinets and hardwood countertops. It offers enough storage space for cooking utensils and supplies and comes equipped with a black inset sink, an induction cooktop, and a full-size fridge that is hidden from view. Hooks, open shelves, and a long ledge make it easy to keep essentials within easy reach, and owners can also add plug-in appliances to add even more functionality to the space.
Photo: Madeiguincho Just like the rest of the house, the bathroom blends modern minimalism with warm, natural wood elements. It features a large shower, a matte black toilet, and a matching black vessel sink mounted on a simple wooden washstand. Above it hangs a round, black-framed mirror. The space is wrapped in contrasting wood finishes, combining light plywood panels on one side with rich vertical timber boards on the other, and a dark charcoal ceiling overhead. And the nicest perk is that it benefits from its own entry door, for direct access from the outside.
With low ceilings and not much space for anything else besides the queen mattresses, the lofts inside the Tow Côja are clearly designed just for sleeping.
There is no mention of whether this particular unit is designed for off-grid living, but typically, Madeiguincho offers a series of self-sufficiency features, such as solar panels, a battery system, rain-collection systems, dry composting toilets, and more.
Cozy, beautifully styled, and highly functional, the Tow Côja tiny home proves that small-space living is not about what you give up when downsizing but rather about concentrating on what really matters. Here’s a Widebody Lamborghini Temerario To Quench Your Tuned Supercar Thirst
21 photos
Photo: Instagram | kfletchphotography
The Lamborghini Temerario has already been visited by the tuning fairy multiple times, and it is not exactly a surprise, given that it debuted more than two years ago, at the 2024 Monterey Car Week, and it entered production at Sant’Agata Bolognese in 2025.
However, not many thing jobs managed to tick the cool and aggressive boxes at the same time. Sure, looks are definitely subjective, but to be honest, this model (and not only) is best left stock. That’s in my opinion, anyway, as my perfectly specced example would be bone stock, with a cool color on the outside, some Alcantara inserts in the cabin, and probably a new set of wheels.
And the latter would likely be where I would draw the line. You know, if I inherited a huge amount of money from a rich uncle I didn’t know existed, or I hit the jackpot, because this is one pricey ride. A brand new Lamborghini Temerario costs from roughly $400,000, but tick some boxes on the options list and get some Ad Personam goodies, and that price will easily climb to over half a million dollars.
Now, while my perfect Temerario would only feature aftermarket wheels, the one pictured in the gallery has much more than that. Images of it were shared by @kfletchphotography on Instagram earlier in the week, and the supercar features a widebody kit from 1016 Industries, AL13 wheels, and was assembled by RDB LA.
Photo: Instagram | kfletchphotography From what we can tell, the front bumper is the OEM element , but there are a few add-ons here that contribute to the supercar’s unique look. There is also a new splitter with blades on the sides, as well as a new hood that is on the more aggressive side of things. The front wheel arches feature some aftermarket elements on them in order to look more muscular, and quite surprisingly, the rear ones haven’t been altered.
The tuning job also includes a new set of side skirt attachments, as well as new trim on the air intakes right in front of the rear wheels. A roof scoop is part of the makeover, and it appears to be functional. The rear deck is now decorated with a large wing, and there is also a new diffuser from what we can tell. Mind you, the back end of this tuned Lamborghini Temerario is not fully visible in these images, but it is also on the more special side of things.
It looks like the ground clearance of this supercar hasn’t been altered during the tuning job. The machine features a yellow look on the outside, has some black details, and rides on new silver wheels that are larger and slightly wider than the OEM ones. Zooming in through the windows on certain pictures reveals the black and yellow interior, which appears to mix leather and Alcantara upholstery, and the Raging Bull’s logo has proudly been embroidered on the headrests.
The partially electrified oily bits haven’t been mentioned in the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page, and even if the powertrain might not have been modded, it’s not like the Lamborghini Temerario is in dire need of more oomph, is it? After all, we are still talking about a modern supercar that has the ability to sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in just 2.7 seconds, and can keep pushing up to 213 mph (343 kph).
Photo: Instagram | kfletchphotography Lamborghini’s Temerario features a 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine and three electric motors, for a total output of 902 horsepower (920 ps/677 kW). The ICE steams out 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) and 530 lb-ft (730 Nm) of torque. The peak thrust is available from 4,000 to 7,000 rpm, and the maximum torque between 9,000 and 9,750 rpm.
The Lamborghini Temerario’s nuts and bolts are shared with the new Audi Nuvolari, and so far, the Raging Bull is offering its new “baby” supercar in a single flavor. However, the second body style, namely the Spyder, is about to join the lineup, and chances are it will reach dealers across the world next summer, and will also touch down officially in North America.
The open-top model will feature a power-retractable roof that should take in the region of 17 seconds to operate, and due to the extra weight, it should be a tiny bit slower than its sibling that features a fixed-roof design. The official unveiling date is being kept a secret for now, just like every detail about it, but it will get the same powertrain as the current Temerario, likely in the same configuration, with identical output and thrust.
Further down the line, Lamborghini is expected to keep expanding the Temerario family with all kinds of different versions and special editions. After all, its predecessors, the Huracan and Gallardo, were offered in all kinds of configurations. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kyle Fletcher (@kfletchphotography)

1958 Chevy Apache With Digital 632 Big Block V8 Carries a 'Visceral Z Camaro' to the 2027 SEMA Show
7 photos
Photo: adry53customs / Instagram
The 2026 SEMA Show finished recently in Las Vegas, Nevada, but its echoes linger on, and some folks are already dreaming about the next year’s projects – including the aftermarket realm aided by the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators when they’re not dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
For example, Timothy Adry Emmanuel, the virtual artist better known as " adry53customs " on social media, continues his dream ride periplus within the CGI car world and digitally joins the SEMA Show craze. Not long ago, he was on point to provide the renderings for the work-in-progress 1987 Chevrolet Camaro dubbed ‘Visceral Z’ by its builders, Snakepit Customs.
The latter is a custom restoration shop in Clermont, Indiana, and they set out to create the Visceral Z from the 1987 Camaro as a rendering-to-reality project that Adry helped bring to life. They showed it at this year’s SEMA Show even though it’s not complete, and when it’s done, it will have a Wegner Automotive LSX 427 with an 8,000-rpm redline, a Harrop Engineering Hurricane ITB intake, a core ECU by HP Tuners, a Radium Engineering fuel system, PWR Advanced Cooling Technology, Valhalla Fabrication custom-built Tri-Y headers and exhaust, plus a lot more.
Yep, the list continues with a 6XD sequential tucked behind the Roadster Shop FastTrack IRS chassis and will roll on Forgeline AL300s in Carbon Black shod in Hoosier Racing Tire Track Attack Pros, while Wilwood Engineering provided the six-piston front and four-piston brakes. Basically, the pixel master thought it was too rad not to give it a custom companion, and cooked up a virtual 1958 Chevrolet Task Force ‘Apache’ pickup truck for hauling duties.
The latter, together with the Camaro, would be ready for next year’s edition of the SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, with the Chevrolet sports car being hauled on a custom trailer by this bespoke widebody truck with staggered wheels and a matching paint job, plus a ZZ632/1000 Chevrolet Performance Big Block V8 from GM Performance under the hood.
The pickup truck has restomod touches all over the place, like the LED headlights and rear lights, but it’s built for the track, above all, even in Imagination Land. As such, it comes severely lowered and equipped with an aerodynamic body kit that could make even the extreme folks over at Liberty Walk a bit envious. There are also matching black alloy wheels with the Camaro, and the livery plus the paint emulates it, too.
So, what do you think? Should they start looking for a potential donor truck and start a new build for the 2027 edition of the SEMA Show? Or is it too extreme even for this great trade event? Audi Will Invest $7 Billion in U.S. Plant, While VW Group Shuts Down Plants in Germany
15 photos
Photo: Audi
Audi is considering a massive $3 billion expansion of its upcoming manufacturing plant in the United States, which could bring an additional 3,000 jobs by 2033. That would be on top of the already planned investment of $4 billion that Audi’s CEO announced last month. This is happening while the Volkswagen Group is making efforts to reduce costs by cutting jobs and shutting down plants in Germany.
Just a couple of weeks after the original announcement, Audi is already planning a Phase 2 expansion before it has even broken ground on its facility, set to be built on a 1,500-acre mega-site in Peach County, located just southwest of Macon in Central Georgia.
Audi's CEO Gernot Dollner joined Donald Trump on stage during a political campaign rally held in Perry, Georgia, just a few miles away from the planned site. During the rally, Trump revealed the initial $4 billion investment plan to the crowd before inviting Audi's CEO up on stage to confirm the information and reveal further details.
Gernot Dollner basically looked like the wrong man at the wrong time, because Volkswagen Group is massively investing in U.S. production while executing just as massive a global cost-cutting process to rescue profitability. Besides, he breached compay policy, which bars executives from making public appearances with political candidates or politicians standing for election within three months of a vote.
Photo: Audi That is because fierce competition coming from China, severe overcapacity in Europe, and collapsing profits have driven the auto giant’s profit margins down to an unsustainable 3.8%. To reverse this, the group’s CEO Oliver Blume has secured stakeholder approval for what is turning out to be the largest, most aggressive structural shakeup the firm has been through in its 87-year history.
Cutting jobs in an oversized company Volkswagen employs nearly 630,000 people worldwide, which is significantly more than its main global rival, Toyota. As of the most recent corporate filings from March 31, 2026, Toyota Motor Corporation employs 390,927 people worldwide.
The German group's board officially doubled its restructuring targets, committing to eliminate 100,000 jobs globally by 2030. That is 15% of its entire workforce. In the meantime, the new plant in America will create a total of 7,500 jobs.
Furthermore, Porsche and Audi's European staff are expected to bear a massive portion of these layoffs to protect the group's cash flow. Volkswagen's management has proposed a strict salary freeze until 2030 for roughly 600,000 employees to combat labor costs.
Photo: Volkswagen In the meantime, Volkswagen’s business in China is a full-blown emergency situation, forcing the automaker to completely abandon its decades-long strategy of using the Asian state as an easy profit engine. For nearly 40 years, China generated massive piles of cash that subsidized the rest of Volkswagen’s global operations.
Volkswagen Group's sales strategy in China is cracking However, right now, that system is falling apart, and the group has to rely on its other largest foreign market, North America. And this is exactly what it is doing now, starting with Audi’s footprint in the U.S., which will help the company offset tariffs imposed on imports.
According to documents from the Mid-Georgia Gateway Development Authority, the footprint will scale significantly over the next decade, Automotive News reports . The process will kick off with the already confirmed $4 billion investment. The plant will open in the early 2030s and create 4,500 jobs.
Phase 2 will bring another $3 billion, according to Automotive News. The production hub is expected to be completed by 2033 with a total of 7,500 jobs and an annual output of 200,000 SUVs. Audi will build its largest, heaviest, and most premium flagship SUVs at the new Georgia facility, with the all-new Q9 leading the pack. The Audi Q7 and Q8 will also roll off the production line of the future Georgia plant.
Photo: Audi The Audi Q5 is expected to join them, since it is the undisputed king of sales in America. Audi sold 46,215 Q5s in 2025 and 33,509 units through the first nine months of this year. Its second best-selling model is about halfway there, with 23,581 examples moved in 2025 and 17,866 units sold in 2026.
Georgia is heavily subsidizing Audi's tariff escape Audi is benefiting from massive financial incentives from the state of Georgia, which is thus securing the mega-plant, starting with nearly one billion dollars in total state aid. First, it is offering a 1,500-acre construction site for free, along with $458 million in state tax incentives.
Furthermore, over $120 million will be allocated for the initial construction, rail link improvements, and environmental cleanups, with another $430 million dedicated to local water infrastructure, road upgrades, utility scaling, and workforce recruitment and training.
Audi has been importing 100% of its U.S. inventory from Europe (sedans, e-tron EVs and large SUVs) and Mexico (Audi Q5 with all its variants). Last year, the tariffs imposed by the Trump administration cost Audi a staggering $1.4 billion.
Photo: Audi To bypass this financial bleed, Audi negotiated a deal with federal officials: the U.S. Commerce Department is expected to drop Audi's EU import tariffs from 15% down to about 10% as a direct reward for making this massive domestic manufacturing investment. Audi had initially pushed for a reduction to 7.5%.
The Ingolstadt-based automaker arrives late at the U.S. party. Its main rivals in the segment have been producing vehicles in the United States for decades. BMW opened its giant Spartanburg plant in South Carolina back in 1994. Mercedes-Benz has had its Tuscaloosa, Alabama hub operating since 1996.

This Brabus G-Wagen 6x6 Deserves Nothing but Respect!
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | brabus
Another day, another tuned G-Wagen from the model’s second generation? Well, yes and no. Yes because it did come from a renowned tuner’s portfolio, and no because it is more of a coachbuilt model rather than a modified one.
As we are certain you already know, the modern-day Mercedes G-Wagen is not offered with six axles, regardless of whether we are talking about a normal Benz or the range-topping Mercedes-AMG G 63. But its predecessor was available in this configuration straight from the factory, looking like an apocalypse-ready vehicle that can conquer the outdoors like a veritable off-roading champ.
Christened the Mercedes-Benz G 63 AMG 6x6 , because the Affalterbach sub-brand was not fully integrated into Mercedes back then, it saw the light of day between 2013 and 2015. Production took place at the Magna Steyr factory in Graz, Austria, and this model was a four-door pickup truck with six axles. It had a front engine and six-wheel drive layout, packing a 5.5-liter twin-turbocharged V8 mated to a 7-speed automatic transmission.
The mill was rated at 536 hp (544 ps/400 kW) and 561 lb-ft (761 Nm) of torque, enabling 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in around eight seconds, and a maximum speed limited to 100 mph (160 kph). Thus, it wasn’t exactly a sprinter disguised as a triathlete, but then again, it did have a curb weight exceeding 4 metric tons (9,000 lbs), and measure a massive 231.3 inches (5,875 mm) in length, 87 inches (2,210 mm) in height, and 83.1 inches (2,110 mm) in width.
Photo: Instagram | brabus As for the Mercedes- AMG G 63 6x6 pictured above, it came from Brabus, and it is called the XLP 6x6 Adventure . It has an upgraded 4.0-liter bi-turbo V8 that produces 789 hp (800 ps/588 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque. The engine allows it to hit 62 mph (100 kph) in 5.8 seconds, and the maximum top speed is 130 mph (210 kph).
Based on the modern-day Mercedes-AMG G 63, the Brabus XLP 6x6 Adventure is a four-door pickup truck with front and rear fender extensions, a roll bar, carbon side walls in the load area, underride guard, skirts at the front and rear, some carbon-made panel parts on the sides, electric running boards, LED lighting, and even a winch with a 4.5-ton (9,921 lbs) capacity, and a plastic cable that is 30 meters (98 feet) in length.
Additional lights, a wind deflector, a roof rack, and other things are also on deck, and this Brabus XLP 6x6 Adventure comes with 9.5x22-inch wheels on all axles, shod in 325/55 tires. The pictured example has a glossy black look, some red details in the Panamericana grille that is decorated with the Brabus logo, a red winch cable, red calipers and suspension, red logos on the sides, wheels, and rear, and a few other goodies. And yes, portal axles are also part of the makeover.
More red accents can be seen on the inside, and these include the trim on the steering wheel, the 12 o’clock marker, the door pins, window and seat controls, air vents, speaker covers, and other things. The leather upholstery is black and has a diamond pattern, there is some extra carbon fiber trim, and we can also see some overhead gauges, as well as a black headliner, and other things that further contribute to the special nature of this heavily modified Mercedes-AMG G 63.
Photo: Instagram | brabus According to the official specs, this model is 243.4 inches (6,183 mm) long, 90.3 inches (2,293 mm) tall, and 86.3 inches (2,192 mm) wide, and tips the scales at over 8,000 pounds net (3,670 kg). It burns the equivalent of 10.7 mpg US (21.9 l/100 km) combined, so it’s not exactly a frugal ride, but then again, you didn’t think it was, did you? As for the average carbon dioxide emissions, these are rated at 420 g/km.
While the standard Mercedes-AMG G 63 has an MSRP of $198,750 attached to it in the United States of America for the 2027 model year, the Brabus XLP 6x6 Adventure is a seven-digit affair. We found the pictured example advertised on the tuner’s official website with an asking price of 1,333,774.61 euros attached to it at the time of writing, and this equals almost $1.5 million at the current exchange rate.
This build is definitely a masterpiece aimed at deep-pocketed enthusiasts, and while it can cope with the great outdoors like a champ, the chances of encountering one of these off the beaten path are close to zero. That’s because this model will mostly be used as a school bus and grocery getter for the most part, and it’s sad, because it deserves to be put through its paces on challenging terrains.
Still, if you paid $1.5 million for your very own Brabus XLP 6x6 Adventure, would you really take it off-roading? And more importantly, would you ever see yourself owning one of these if money were the least of your worries? I would! View this post on Instagram A post shared by BRABUS (@brabus)

Chicago Dealer Selling Lamborghini Urus for Less Money Than a New Mercedes SUV
14 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
Between us, it is not exactly the Urus SE Performante that we are looking at here, which is Lamborghini’s latest take on its popular model.
This one debuted earlier this year, and it remains the only Urus currently in production. It offers 801 hp (598 kW/812 ps) and 738 pound-feet (1,000 Nm) of torque in total from its upgraded 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 plug-in hybrid powertrain. It an travel for 37 miles (60 km) in the EV mode, hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 3.4 seconds, and has a 194 mph (312 kph) top speed.
It is not even the Urus SE Performante’s predecessor, the Lamborghini Urus SE , which is one-tenth of a second slower than its successor and has an identical top speed. This version of the exotic crossover, which shares its roots with the demised Volkswagen Touareg, the aging Bentley Bentayga, and the old Audi Q7, among others, has 789 hp (589 kW/800 ps) and 701 pound-feet (950 Nm) of torque combined.
As you can likely tell from the images shared in the gallery, you are not even looking at the discontinued S or Performante versions of the Lamborghini Urus. These featured no electrification, came with 657 hp (490 kW/666 ps) and 627 pound-feet (850 Nm) of torque on tap. The Urus Performante hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 3.3 seconds, identical to the electrified Urus SE Performante, and the Urus S is 0.2 seconds slower. The top speed is 190 and 189 mph (306-305 kph), respectively.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago By elimination, what we are left with is the original Lamborghini Urus . You know, as in the model that debuted back in 2017, hitting the assembly line that same year. It too featured a V8 with twin turbocharging and a 4.0-liter displacement, which was good for 641 hp (478 kW/650 ps). At 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque, the thrust was identical to the S and Performante versions, and this model needed 3.6 seconds to reach 62 mph from a standstill, reaching a top speed of 190 mph (306 kph).
The pictured example is a 2020 model year car that features a Grigio Nimbus Metallic paint finish on the outside. But why is it orange? Because it has been wrapped. It also has a glossy black wrap on the hood and roof, as well as on other exterior components, rides on black V-spoke wheels, and sports red brake calipers. And for what it’s worth, it definitely looks very good on the outside, doesn’t it?
But what about the interior, you ask? Well, here, the pre-facelifted Lamborghini Urus in question has black leather upholstery with plenty of red stitching for contrast. It also features the Italian flag motif on the steering wheel, some metal trim on the dashboard, the Raging Bull’s corporate logo embroidered into the headrests, black pillars, a black headliner, a panoramic roof, multi-zone climate control, and three screens, including one for the HVAC system.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago In one of the images, we can see the check engine light illuminated in the digital gauge cluster, though the vendor hasn’t said anything about it. In fact, other than the mileage, asking price, and the fact that it has been wrapped, it did not have anything else to say about this machine. The vehicle had in the region of 49,000 miles (~79,000 km) under its belt at the time of cataloging, so it has seen some action over the years.
A 2020 model year Lamborghini Urus usually sells from $140,000 to $220,000 in today’s used car market in the United States of America. Examples with 40,000-50,000+ (64,000-79,000+) miles are considered high-mileage cars, and they sit at the lower end of the market, whereas those that have fewer than 15,000 miles (24,000 km) tend to reach the $200K mark and break into it.
Therefore, the Urus pictured in the gallery should not be on the pricey side of things. But is that really the case? Well, we found it advertised by @motorcarsofchicago on Instagram with an asking price of $169,995 at the time of writing, and it is up to you to decide whether it is worth that sum.
As far as the Mercedes SUV reference in the title, this Urus costs less than a brand-new Mercedes-AMG G 63, which has an MSRP of $198,750, and it is also more affordable than the Mercedes-Maybach GLS 680, which starts at $185,000. Sure, these may not be its rivals, because the Urus takes on the Ferrari Purosangue and Aston Martin DBX, but price-wise, it is more affordable than some new crossovers/SUVs.
Now, if you have that kind of money lying around and the desire to park a Lamborghini Urus in your driveway, the you should reach out to the selling dealer with an offer. Who knows, maybe you might be able to score this 2020 Lamborghini Urus for less money than advertised. After all, what’s the worse that they can do? Say no? Liberty Walk Founder Says This Tuned Ferrari F40 Is His Favorite Car. Do You Dig the Makeover?
6 photos
Photo: Instagram | libertywalkkato
The Ferrari F40 may have been dead and buried for three decades, but it continues to make headlines today, and you can understand why, can’t you?
If you said no, then you may want to throw away your petrolhead license, as you clearly do not use it. This model remains a motoring icon, and it is one of the best vehicles the Prancing Horse has ever made. On top of that, it is the last model approved by Enzo Ferrari himself before he passed away in 1988.
Ferrari’s F40 may look quite modern on the outside, but it was actually developed in the 1980s. It hit the production line back in 1987 at the Maranello factory in Italy, and was discontinued 9 years later, in 1996, after over 1,300 units were put together. The number includes the GTE, Competizione, and LM models.
Designed by Pietro Camardella under the close watch of Aldo Brovarone at Pininfarina, with Nicola Materazzi being the chief engineer, the supercar was offered in a single body style, a two-door berlinetta. The coupe had a longitudinally-mounted engine mounted in the middle toward the rear, right behind the passenger compartment, which drove the rear wheels through a five-speed manual transmission.
Photo: Instagram | libertywalkkato Given that it was born in the 1980s, some might think that the Ferrari F40 could feature a V12, or perhaps a V8 with no forced induction. But it actually features twin turbocharging, and if you know your classic supercars, then you remember that the mill of choice had a 2.9-liter displacement, pumping out 471 hp (352 kW/478 ps) and 426 lb-ft (577 Nm) of torque.
According to the spec sheet, the 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) acceleration took just 4.1 seconds, which is highly impressive for something that it almost four decades old. Flat-out, the F40 did 201 mph (324 kph), and if you are curious about the standing quarter mile, then you should know that it completed it in 11.9 seconds.
Alongside the 288 GTO, the F50, Enzo, and LaFerrari, the Ferrari F40 is considered to be one of the best machines ever signed by the Prancing Horse. Something like this usually fetches between $2.5 and $5.5 million in today’s market, and an ultra-low-mileage example changed hands for over $8.3 million recently.
As a result, the Ferrari F40 is not exactly the kind of car that deserves to get a tuning job. However, that does not mean that there are no modified examples out there, because some of them have been visited by the tuning fairy, including the one pictured in the gallery, which has got to be one of the most famous tuned F40s out there.
Mind you, it’s not a new project, because it has been around for quite a few years now, and we have dedicated several stories to it so far. And as it happens, this machine recently smiled for the camera again, with the images being shared on social media by Liberty Walk’s founder recently, who admitted that this is his favorite car.
Photo: Instagram | libertywalkkato We can understand why, because the Ferrari F40 remains a dream machine, though purists will likely not agree with the widebody makeover. The fender flares, new lip attached to the front bumper, some extras at the rear, a large diffuser, and a big rear wing, alongside a set of beefy side skirts, make up the aftermarket redesign.
This thing also has three center-mounted exhaust tips that are bigger than the OEM ones, a retuned suspension, new wheels, and a white look sprinkled with some decals. The interior is home to red bucket seats and some other extras, and some might argue that it rocks this design perfectly, whereas others would definitely agree to disagree.
The purist crowd may definitely want to look away, because they would describe this build using one word: sacrilege. Or perhaps a synonym of that word. However, the attention to detail is definitely there, and to be honest, it would not take that much to revert this Ferrari F40 back to its original condition.
I’ve always had a soft spot for most things Liberty Walk, and while this tuner’s builds may usually follow the same widebody, stanced recipe, it is this exact bundle that has made them famous. Therefore, while I would probably want to hate this modified Ferrari F40 , I simply can’t, because to me, it looks almost perfect. After all, what’s wrong with a widebody classic exotic model that sits closer to the ground and rides on new wheels?
This comment will probably spark some hate toward me in the comments area, but hey, we all have our soft spots and simple pleasures when it comes to the car game, don’t we? That said, feel free to speak your mind below about this tuned Ferrari F40, regardless of whether you hate it or love it. But honestly, do you really hate it? Upcoming Mercedes-AMG CLE 63 S With V8 Gets Rid of the Camouflage and Is Unmasked in Fantasy Land
9 photos
Photo: avarvarii / Instagram
Back in late 2023, Mercedes-Benz decided to showcase to the world the new Mercedes-Benz CLE grand tourer class with a C236 coupe and the A236 cabriolet body styles – they consolidated the former C-Class and E-Class sports cars into a single series aimed at combating the BMW 4 Series.
The CLE Coupe was introduced to replace both the C-Class Coupe and E-Class Coupe as part of Mercedes' focus on reimagining the model range – but at least they didn’t kill all of them as Audi did with the A5 series, which is now a fastback sedan and a station wagon instead of a coupe, cabriolet, and fastback.
Still a product of its times, the new Mercedes-Benz CLE grand tourer gained a wide array of powertrains: mild hybrid diesel on the CLE 220d, a mild hybrid turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four, a mild hybrid turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six, plus a CLE 300e plug-in hybrid setup. The AMG version was initially launched as the Mercedes-AMG CLE 53 with the mild-hybrid AMG-enhanced M256 3.0-liter inline six-cylinder engine packing an exhaust gas turbocharger and electric auxiliary compressor.
It also had the AMG Performance 4Matic+ fully variable all-wheel drive and active rear-axle steering, plus the distinctive AMG styling, but it doesn’t actually pack a massive punch: 443 hp and up to 433 lb-ft or 587 Nm with overboost for ten seconds. Of course, soon enough there were ample rumors about the CLE 63 going against the inline-four C-Class PHEV setup with a return to V8 form.
The news outlets exploded this year as tension began building up for the mighty AMG – and Mercedes released part of it in early September 2026 when it unleashed the hard-to-pronounce Mercedes-AMG CLE 646 Spezialanfertigung (Special Edition) as the latest entry into the bespoke Mythos series, with the 4.0‑liter V8 biturbo AMG engine rocking 637 hp under the hood and sending them only to the rear wheels.
Alas, the new model is actually something that only collectors and one-percenter enthusiasts can get due to the rumored $800k price and the ultra-exclusive production run of just 30 units. As such, once the hype went down, fans were back to square one, dreaming and hoping that a Mercedes-AMG CLE 63 or 63 S is coming to them without the E Performance moniker but instead with a V8.
Well, the spy photographers are now busy catching the Mercedes-AMG Black Series while out testing, yet a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators can’t stop dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI because they’re thinking that a Mercedes-AMG CLE 63 is also around the corner.
More precisely, Avarvarii Automotive Artworks (also known as ' avarvarii ' on social media) has taken a thorough, in-depth CGI look at AMG's upcoming plans and came up with this – the unmasked CLE 63. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Avarvarii Automotive Artworks (@avarvarii)

Ford Mustang Dragster Races Corvette ZR1 Down the 1/4-Mile, Time To Place Your Bets
7 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Wheels
General Motors has done a fantastic job with the C8-generation Chevrolet Corvette , as not only is the lineup vaster than ever, but it is also more exciting than it has ever been.
The family comprises six distinct versions of the latest model year, and it is the same Stingray that kicks things off. And it packs a new motor, in case you forgot. The small-block V8 has a 6.7-liter displacement this time around, pushing out 535 hp (399 kW/453 ps) and 520 lb-ft (705 Nm) of torque. With the Z51 Performance Pack, which is optional, it needs just 2.8 seconds to reach 60 mph (97 kph). Flat-out, it will do over 200 mph (322+ kph).
That’s basically modern-day supercar territory in something that starts at $71,300 (MSRP). And even its predecessor came with up to 495 hp (369 kW /502 ps), with the 6.2-liter V8 rocketing it to 60 mph in 2.9 seconds. The Grand Sport is next in line, packs the same mill as its lesser sibling, and starts at $86,300. The E-Ray’s successor is the Grand Sport X, and this model comes from $110,000, boasting 721 hp (538 kW/731 ps) in total, and dropping the sprint time to a neck-snapping 2.4 seconds.
Further up, we find the Z06, with its 670 hp (499 kW/679 ps), 2.6 seconds required to hit 60 mph, and an MSRP of $121,800. Sitting at the very top of the lineup is the ZR1X , which features the electric assistance from the discontinued E-Ray, and the Z06’s 5.5-liter V8, albeit with twin turbos. The result is 1,250 hp (933 kW/1,268 ps) and 937 pound-feet (1,270 Nm) of torque in total. 0-60 mph takes 1.89 seconds, the top speed stands at 233 mph (375 kph), and the 1/4-mile is an 8.99-second affair at 157 mph (253 kph).
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Wheels Pricing in this case commences at $227,800, but good luck trying to land one for a bit more over the MSRP, because the dealer markups are insane. The same goes for the lesser Chevy Corvette ZR1. But why haven’t we mentioned it until now? Because it is one of the stars of the video embedded at the bottom of the page.
It kicks off at $198,000, and even if that may be a lot of money, it can actually give supercars that are three times more expensive a real run for their money. From 0 to 60 mph, the C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 needs just 2.3 seconds. It has 1,064 hp (794 kW/1,079 ps) and 828 lb-ft (1,123 Nm) of torque, and packs a 5.5-liter flat-plane crank V8 with two turbochargers. The top speed is 233 mph (375 kph), and the quarter mile time is 9.6 seconds, with an exit speed of 150 mph (241 kph).
Thus, one must have an insane build if they want to beat the Chevy Corvette ZR1 into submission, but can a Ford Mustang make it to the list? Well, not if we are talking about a bone-stock example, regardless of whether we are talking about the modern-day S650 or the previous-generation, the S550.
This one is part of the latter, and it seems that it started life in the GT configuration , packing a Coyote V8 with 460 horsepower (340 kW/462 ps) available via the right pedal and 420 pound-feet (570 Nm) of torque. The acceleration from 0 to 60 mph took 4.4 seconds, and that makes it a lot slower than its ad-hoc rival, the Corvette ZR1.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Wheels Mind you, one does not have to be a connoisseur to tell that the Ford Mustang GT in question has been visited by the tuning fairy. Not only that, but it is basically a dragster disguised as a muscle car rather than the other way around. It boasts drag radials, has a massive bulge on the hood, and also packs a mandatory parachute to help it stop faster.
We would like to tell you that it has X horsepower and Y torque, but the truth is that we have no idea just how punchy this machine is. And by the looks of it, it is a proper rival to the C8 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 in a head-to-head battle down the quarter mile from a standing start. But is it really anyone’s game?
That is for you to find out by scrolling down to the video shared by Wheels on YouTube and embedded at the bottom of this story. The footage is a little over one and a half minutes long, and if you don’t want to waste your time and jump right into the battle, then you should know that the action starts at the 1:28 mark.
Before clicking the play button, which one of these machines do you think came out victorious? Was it the modern-day ZR1 or the Mustang dragster ? Now, head on down to find out if you were right.
